Add installs one bonus attribute from the offered choices, limited by the [Enchanter facility — name pending]'s BP capacity (row 54). Rarity after Add = the higher of (a) the minimum rarity of the rarest line on the item and (b) the lowest rarity whose normal budget holds the total BP (Uncommon 100 / Rare 150 / Epic 200; 2H doubled). Rarity never goes down (Remove and Modify-down keep it). Example: Common sword + STR T1 (50 BP) = Uncommon; + HP T1 = 100 = Uncommon (full); + AGI T1 = 150 = Rare; + DEX T1 = 200 = Epic (max level only). Add refuses a family already on the item (use Modify). Fortune is never offered (row 58). Raising rarity charges the catch-up fee (row 48); reaching Epic also charges the Epic step fee (row 57).

Add = pick 1 of the offered eligible attributes (count by level, row 53). Remove = delete one line for a small gold fee, nothing back, rarity stays. Reroll = shows a few fixed options at the same tier; the player picks one or keeps the old line (cost paid either way); options are fixed by the item + its reroll count, so leaving and rejoining never changes them. Modify = move one line one tier up or down in its family; up costs the new tier's Essences and must fit capacity and unlocked tiers; down costs a little gold, no refund. Gold (starting value, Simulator to tune) = floor(item base value x 0.30 x (1 + item level / 25) x factor x (1 - [Enchanter facility — name pending] discount)); factor: Add = tier number (T1 1 ... Essences: T1 = 1 Uncommon, T2 = 2 Uncommon, T3 = 2 Rare, T4 = 2 Epic; Reroll = 1 Essence of the line's rarity. The discount is gold only.

When enchanting raises an item's rarity, the player pays the upgrade cost difference they skipped: what the item's Blacksmith upgrades from its starting level to its current level cost at the new rarity, minus what they cost at the old rarity (gold + gear-upgrade materials). Every route (upgrade then enchant, or enchant then upgrade) costs the same total. Each item stores one extra saved number: the item level it dropped or was bought at. How it is worked out: for each level from the item's starting level to its current level, (normal Blacksmith upgrade cost at the new rarity - cost at the old rarity), gold and gear materials, using the player's current Blacksmith gold discount. Downgrading an item below its starting level lowers the starting level to the new level. Items that existed before this is built start at their current level, so they never owe a fee (ASSUMPTION - user to confirm).
